messages.author: 84d40346d2b44e80
messages.subject: Installing all packages up front
parts:
Hi All,

I'm installing Rattle on a server & want to make sure that it gets all the files that it needs in advance so that users don't waste disk space in their own areas. I used:

install.packages("rattle", dependencies=c("Depends", "Suggests"))

but it still asked me for quite a few packages when I started using it such as XML, pmml, cairoDevice and ellipse. It also gave GTK error messages until I had installed all the ones that it asked for when I first started it. What am I doing wrong?

Thanks,
Bob

messages.author: 6f733a9cb68b4415
messages.subject: RE: Installing all packages up front [SEC=UNOFFICIAL]
parts:
Hi Bob,
 
Trouble is, Im not sure your doing anything wrong. I too have had this problem, and raised it with Graham. Ive tried a few other ways over time, but so far, none have totally worked.
 
I did try once to write a piece of code that inserted every package that rattle used into the install packages dependences command, but i am not a good enough programmer. I have usually just tried to run every possible item within Rattle, to get them all. But this is not a problem specific to Rattle, I have found this issue with trying to get other dependences with out packages too. 
 
I do try a cheat now, using RStudio, I select every package, and see any errors that it brings up, and load those packages. While its not much different, it is easier to work in, when searching for missing packages.
 
Regards
Tony

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Installing all packages up front [SEC=UNOFFICIAL]
parts:
Thanks for the feedback Bob, Tony.

As best I can tell what you are doing should work.

From http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/index.html we can see that the mentioned packages (XML, pmml, cairoDevice,...) are certainly in the Suggests list. As far as I know that should mean that the install.packages command Bob used should pull them all in. I'm pretty sure that it does it for me on Ubuntu. Could it be a temporary network connectivity issue?

If it helps, I attach some code that will attempt to load absolutely everything potentially used by Rattle:

> source("rattle.install.packages.R")
> rattle.install.packages()

Hopefully this finds all dependencies for rattle and installs them (if not already installed) and also updates all installed packages.

Hope that helps.

Regards,
Graham

> install.packages("RGtk2")

RGtk2 is a rather key dependency for Rattle. Have you tried installing it from the R console rather than from within RStudio. I have seen that RStudio does some extra work with libraries and paths on starting up - and I wonder if somehow that interferes with the install of RGtk2 (or with the underlying GTK+ zip file that is separately downloaded and installed for you as part of the install).

You could also try installing GTK+ manually, unzipping the downloaded GTK+ zip file and adding the location to the PATH variable. 

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com
